scenes.text: The Moon is slowly running away from Earth.
Every year it drifts about three point eight centimeters farther away.
We know because Apollo astronauts left mirrors on the Moon.
Scientists fire lasers at them and time how long the light takes to bounce back.
The cause is ocean tides, which slowly push the Moon into a wider orbit.
Did you know astronauts left mirrors up there?

title: The Moon is running away from us 🌕
caption: The Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year. We measure it by bouncing lasers off mirrors the Apollo astronauts left behind.
